#!/usr/bin/env node
/***
 * MARK: run-tests.mjs
 * @description Cross-platform full-project verification gate: the same seven
 *   checks the old `run-tests.sh` ran plus the Container Tests branch, the
 *   Frontend Build branch (exercises the deprecation gate), the Dependency
 *   Audit Gate, the Proof Hygiene branch, and the Binary Guard branch, in a
 *   single overlap window
 *   (the two unit suites
 *   alone take ~2x35s sequentially, so overlapping keeps the wall near one
 *   suite), with identical `Running <name>... PASS/FAIL (<s>s)` lines and exit semantics —
 *   but driven by Node (`node:child_process`, no shell), so it runs on
 *   Linux, macOS, and Windows with only Node + npm installed. Shells out
 *   only to `npm`/Node/Docker; the two environment-conditional branches
 *   report SKIP instead of failing when their runtime is absent (Security
 *   Script Tests without `bash`, Container Tests without a Docker daemon).
 *   The fast branches share one overlap window; the Canary Tests branch runs
 *   alone afterwards (see splitGatePhases) — same suites, same exit
 *   semantics, but the heaviest branch never shares CPUs with the unit
 *   suites. Fail-fast is ON by default (see resolveFailFast): when the fast
 *   phase fails, the gate writes its verdict (`verdict.json` plus one

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
  its own design section (§7).

## 2. Survey analysis (SURVEY.md) — unanswered, with recommendations

The grill survey exists but `answers` is `{}` — nobody has answered yet. The
plan below assumes the **recommended** answer for each question (marked ★) and
notes where the code must keep the other option open. Before implementation
starts, re-run the grill (or get 5 minutes of the requester's time) to confirm;
each recommendation is one line to flip.

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
  its own design section (§7).

### 3.4 Key invariants to preserve

1. **Single-branch resolvers**: `resolveDocsPath` / `resolveKainbainDir` stay
   the only place that maps (project, cwd) → absolute path. No caller
   hand-builds `cwd + "/docs"`.
2. **Redacted-at-rest URLs**: stored repo URLs are redacted; live git reads
   `.git/config` (see `detectGitRemote`, `redactCredentials`).
3. **Never-lose-work git hygiene**: recovery branches, no force-delete of
   unpushed work, `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction rules — the docs worktree inherits
   all of it.
4. **Runner ships standalone**: runner-side helpers cannot import backend code
   (the `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` duplication is intentional).
5. **Tolerant reads, strict writes**: resolvers degrade to defaults on garbage;
   write paths 400 with `INVALID_*` codes (see `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`

## 4. Target design (v1)

### 4.1 Data model — new project fields

```text
project.docsRepo: {
  url: string|null        # credential-REDACTED remote URL, e.g. "https://git.example.com/me/proj-kb.git"
  localPath: string|null  # backend-side checkout of the docs repo (absolute).
                          # For adopted/local setups: a path the operator gives or
                          # KainBain provisions next to cwd. For remote-backed: the
                          # backend's own clone/mirror location.
  branchMode: "synced"    # v1 fixed: docs repo carries the same kb/<taskId>
                          # branches as the code repo (see §4.3). Reserved for
                          # future "single-branch" mode.
  # auth: decided by research spike R1. Preferred: reuse the host's existing
  # credential mechanism per-remote (git credential helper / env), with an
  # optional per-project docs credential slot when R1 shows a gap.
}
```

- Absent `docsRepo` (legacy projects, default) = today's behaviour, byte for
  byte. This is the compatibility anchor: every new branch is `if
  (hasDocsRepo(project)) … else …today…`.
- Validation mirrors `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`:
  `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite` → 400 `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes; tolerant
  `normalizeDocsRepoSettings` for reads.
- One docs repo per project enforced (q7): backend refuses a `localPath`/`url`
  already claimed by another project (clear 409 message), until sharing is
  designed.

### 4.2 Backend layout — "KainBain home" split

Introduce one concept: **`kainbainHome/projectCwd` split**.

- Today: `projectCwd` serves as *both* code home and KainBain home
  (`<cwd>/docs/tasks`, `<cwd>/.kainbain/*`).
- With `docsRepo`: code home stays `projectCwd`; KainBain home becomes the
  docs-repo checkout (`docsRepo.localPath` on the backend).
- Implementation: add `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)` =
  `docsRepo.localPath || projectCwd`, then re-point `resolveDocsPath` and
  `resolveKainbainDir` at it (they already take `(cwd, project)` — the
  signature barely changes; internally `cwd` becomes "kainbain home").
  All downstream consumers (`taskDocsFiles`, `taskWorkspace`,
  `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `reportRelPath`, …) inherit the move with no edits —
  this is the "make change easy" payoff.
- `ensureDocsLink` / centralised-docs symlink: when `docsRepo` is set, the
  `<cwd>/docs` symlink is **not created** (stealth, q5) and
  `centralizedDocs` is ignored for that project (documented precedence:
  `docsRepo` > `centralizedDocs:false` > symlink). The docs checkout itself is
  a real git repo, not a symlink.
- `.gitignore` management: today KainBain writes ignore entries for
  `docs/tasks/` + `.kainbain/` into the main repo. With `docsRepo`, nothing is
  written into the main repo (q5 ★); equivalent ignores (if still needed) live
  in the docs repo. Audit every ignore-writing call site in Phase 1.
- `project.json`: per q1 ★, the authoritative copy lives in the docs repo
  (`<docsHome>/.kainbain/project.json`… or flattened — decided in Phase 1;
  recommend keeping the `.kainbain/` layout identical so resolvers don't fork).
  The backend's project *registry* (`projectRegistry.js`) keeps a pointer so
  `scanProjects` still finds the project. Main repo keeps zero files.

### 4.3 Branching — synced task branches across two repos

- The docs repo carries the **same branch names** as the code repo:
  `kb/<taskId>` per task, same default branch. "Synced" means: created from
  the same base event, checked out/created together at stage pickup
  (`ensureTaskBranch` gains a docs-repo twin), and pushed together at handoff.
- Merge/review semantics stay code-repo-driven: the Merge stage merges code;
  docs branches merge (or fast-forward) alongside so docs history tracks task
  history. Exact merge coupling (same commit message? docs-merge part of the
  merge stage, or lazy?) is decided in design task D3 (Phase 1) — v1 default:
  docs branch is merged/fast-forwarded by the same stage right after the code
  merge, failures reported but never blocking the code merge verdict… or
  blocking — D3 decides with a written rationale.
- Runner workdir layout becomes a pair:
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` (code worktree, as today) +
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>-docs` (docs worktree, same branch name), each with
  its own mirror (`mirrors/<code-slug>`, `mirrors/<docs-slug>`).
  `prepareWorkdir` grows a `docsRepoUrl` option; eviction/recovery/reap logic
  treats the pair atomically (evict/reap both, park both).
- `syncTaskDocs` becomes a no-op source change: with docsRepo, task docs live
  *in* the docs worktree already — the copy step is skipped and
  `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` points at the docs worktree path. `collectTaskFiles`
  reads from the docs worktree. `commitAndPush` commits+pushes **both**
  worktrees (docs first or code first — D3 decides; recommend docs-first so a
  half-pushed state never shows code without its docs… or code-first — D3
  writes the rationale either way).

### 4.4 Auth (pending spike R1 — shape, not final)

- Backend git ops and runner `runGit` both rely on ambient credentials today
  (live `.git/config` remotes + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` fail-fast). The docs
  remote must authenticate the same way wherever possible (same host ⇒ same
  credential helper ⇒ zero new secrets UI).
- If R1 finds runners/hosts where ambient auth can't cover a second remote,
  add an optional per-project docs credential stored server-side, injected via
  `GIT_ASKPASS`/header at clone/fetch time, never persisted into `.git/config`,
  never logged (extend `redactCredentials` coverage + a redaction test).
- Hard rule: docs-repo credentials must never leak into the main repo, task
  docs, logs, or claim payloads. Spike R1 must name the exact mechanism before
  Phase 2 starts.

### Phase 1 — Make change easy (backend seams, no behaviour change)

Goal: after Phase 1, switching a project's KainBain home is a **one-line
resolver change**, fully covered by tests, with zero user-visible difference.

- **D1. Introduce `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)`** (new module,
  e.g. `api/kainbainHome.js`, mirroring `docsPath.js`/`kainbainDir.js`
  conventions incl. JSDoc `MARK:` blocks). Initially returns `projectCwd`
  always. Re-point `resolveDocsPath` and `resolveKainbainDir` internals at it.
  Unit tests: legacy projects unchanged; explicit cases for the future
  docs-home branch (written now, enabled when the field exists).
- **D2. Fix census strays (from R3)**: route any hand-built docs/state paths
  through the resolvers. Each fix: regression test proving identical output
  before/after.
- **D3. Write the two-repo execution ADR** (design doc under `docs/`):
  branch-sync coupling, merge-stage semantics, commit/push order, failure
  taxonomy (what happens when docs push fails but code push succeeds, and vice

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
  its own design section (§7).

## 2. Survey analysis (SURVEY.md) — unanswered, with recommendations

| # | Question | Recommended answer ★ | Why / plan impact |
|---|----------|----------------------|-------------------|
| q1 | What lives in the docs repo? | ★ **Everything KainBain**: task docs (`docs/tasks/*`), plans, reports, **and** KainBain settings/state (`.kainbain/` contents: `project.json`, sessions, worktrees, quarantine) | Stealth requires zero KainBain traces in the main repo (q5). Splitting settings from docs would leave a decision matrix in every resolver. One "KainBain home" location keeps `resolveDocsPath`/`resolveKainbainDir` a single-branch change. If q1 instead resolves to "task docs only", Phase 3 still works: `project.json` stays in main repo and only the docs resolvers move — the seam is the same. |
| q2 | Where in the import/create UI? | ★ **Tucked under an 'Advanced' section** on *both* create and import dialogs | Task text says "as an advance option" and "allowed from the default when you import/create". Advanced-collapsed keeps the simple form simple (existing dialogs are minimal: name+remote, path+name) while satisfying "from the default". | q3 | Auth for the (private) docs repo? | ★ **Separate login details just for the docs repo** (stored credential, optional: fall back to same-as-main when blank) | Main repo may be public/shared with no credential while docs repo is private, or the two live on different hosts.   established validation/test pattern to copy).

### 3.2 Runner — adjacent checkout and synced branches

- `runner/project.js` — `prepareWorkdir({ repoUrl, localPath, workRoot,
  taskId })`: clone-mode mirror at `<workRoot>/mirrors/<slug>` (+
  `refreshMirror`) or adopt-mode local path; per-task worktree
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` on branch `kb/<taskId>` (+
  `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, LRU eviction under `WORKTREE_CAP`,
  `kb-recovery/*` parking). `syncTaskDocs` copies
  `<primaryCwd>/docs/tasks/<id>` into the worktree; `writeClaimTaskAssets`
  covers remote runners; `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` mirrors the backend
  resolver (deliberately duplicated — "the Runner ships without the backend
  tree"). `collectTaskFiles` in `runner/daemon.js` ships worktree files back.
- `runner/gitOps.js` — `commitAndPush` / `integrateUpstream`: stage-end handoff
  pushes the worktree (code + docs together today).
- Runner git runs with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, 60s budget, per-workdir
  serialisation, stale-lock recovery (`RunnerGitError` codes). The docs
  checkout must reuse `runGit`, not invent a second git path.
- Runner ↔ backend file transfer for task docs goes through the worktree +
  claim payloads (`taskFiles`, `taskAssets`), not through direct docs-repo
  access — this is what lets a remote runner work with no primary checkout.

- `frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx` — New Project modal (name + git
  remote) and Add Existing Project modal (path + display name + KainBain
  folder). No "Advanced" disclosure exists yet — one must be added (q2).
- `frontend/src/components/settings/PathsAndReposSection.jsx` (+
  `ProjectSettingsForm.jsx`) — Files & Repositories block: cwd, notes symlink,
  docs folder name, KainBain folder name, centralised-docs toggle, git URL,

  for existing projects.

### 3.4 Key invariants to preserve

1. **Single-branch resolvers**: `resolveDocsPath` / `resolveKainbainDir` stay
   the only place that maps (project, cwd) → absolute path. No caller
   hand-builds `cwd + "/docs"`.
2. **Redacted-at-rest URLs**: stored repo URLs are redacted; live git reads
   `.git/config` (see `detectGitRemote`, `redactCredentials`).
3. **Never-lose-work git hygiene**: recovery branches, no force-delete of
   unpushed work, `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction rules — the docs worktree inherits
   all of it.
4. **Runner ships standalone**: runner-side helpers cannot import backend code
   (the `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` duplication is intentional).
5. **Tolerant reads, strict writes**: resolvers degrade to defaults on garbage;
   write paths 400 with `INVALID_*` codes (see `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`
   pattern).

## 4. Target design (v1)

### 4.1 Data model — new project fields

```text
project.docsRepo: {
  url: string|null        # credential-REDACTED remote URL, e.g. "https://git.example.com/me/proj-kb.git"
  localPath: string|null  # backend-side checkout of the docs repo (absolute).
                          # For adopted/local setups: a path the operator gives or
                          # KainBain provisions next to cwd. For remote-backed: the
                          # backend's own clone/mirror location.
  branchMode: "synced"    # v1 fixed: docs repo carries the same kb/<taskId>
                          # branches as the code repo (see §4.3). Reserved for
                          # future "single-branch" mode.
  # auth: decided by research spike R1. Preferred: reuse the host's existing
  # credential mechanism per-remote (git credential helper / env), with an
  # optional per-project docs credential slot when R1 shows a gap.
}
```

- Absent `docsRepo` (legacy projects, default) = today's behaviour, byte for
  byte. This is the compatibility anchor: every new branch is `if
  (hasDocsRepo(project)) … else …today…`.
- Validation mirrors `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`:
  `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite` → 400 `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes; tolerant
  `normalizeDocsRepoSettings` for reads.
- One docs repo per project enforced (q7): backend refuses a `localPath`/`url`
  already claimed by another project (clear 409 message), until sharing is
  designed.

### 4.2 Backend layout — "KainBain home" split

Introduce one concept: **`kainbainHome/projectCwd` split**.

- Today: `projectCwd` serves as *both* code home and KainBain home
  (`<cwd>/docs/tasks`, `<cwd>/.kainbain/*`).
- With `docsRepo`: code home stays `projectCwd`; KainBain home becomes the
  docs-repo checkout (`docsRepo.localPath` on the backend).
- Implementation: add `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)` =
  `docsRepo.localPath || projectCwd`, then re-point `resolveDocsPath` and
  `resolveKainbainDir` at it (they already take `(cwd, project)` — the
  signature barely changes; internally `cwd` becomes "kainbain home").
  All downstream consumers (`taskDocsFiles`, `taskWorkspace`,
  `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `reportRelPath`, …) inherit the move with no edits —
  this is the "make change easy" payoff.
- `ensureDocsLink` / centralised-docs symlink: when `docsRepo` is set, the
  `<cwd>/docs` symlink is **not created** (stealth, q5) and
  `centralizedDocs` is ignored for that project (documented precedence:
  `docsRepo` > `centralizedDocs:false` > symlink). The docs checkout itself is
  a real git repo, not a symlink.
- `.gitignore` management: today KainBain writes ignore entries for
  `docs/tasks/` + `.kainbain/` into the main repo. With `docsRepo`, nothing is
  written into the main repo (q5 ★); equivalent ignores (if still needed) live
  in the docs repo. Audit every ignore-writing call site in Phase 1.
- `project.json`: per q1 ★, the authoritative copy lives in the docs repo
  (`<docsHome>/.kainbain/project.json`… or flattened — decided in Phase 1;
  recommend keeping the `.kainbain/` layout identical so resolvers don't fork).
  The backend's project *registry* (`projectRegistry.js`) keeps a pointer so
  `scanProjects` still finds the project. Main repo keeps zero files.

### 4.3 Branching — synced task branches across two repos

- The docs repo carries the **same branch names** as the code repo:
  `kb/<taskId>` per task, same default branch. "Synced" means: created from
  the same base event, checked out/created together at stage pickup
  (`ensureTaskBranch` gains a docs-repo twin), and pushed together at handoff.
- Merge/review semantics stay code-repo-driven: the Merge stage merges code;
  docs branches merge (or fast-forward) alongside so docs history tracks task
  history. Exact merge coupling (same commit message? docs-merge part of the
  merge stage, or lazy?) is decided in design task D3 (Phase 1) — v1 default:
  docs branch is merged/fast-forwarded by the same stage right after the code
  merge, failures reported but never blocking the code merge verdict… or
  blocking — D3 decides with a written rationale.
- Runner workdir layout becomes a pair:
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` (code worktree, as today) +
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>-docs` (docs worktree, same branch name), each with
  its own mirror (`mirrors/<code-slug>`, `mirrors/<docs-slug>`).
  `prepareWorkdir` grows a `docsRepoUrl` option; eviction/recovery/reap logic
  treats the pair atomically (evict/reap both, park both).
- `syncTaskDocs` becomes a no-op source change: with docsRepo, task docs live
  *in* the docs worktree already — the copy step is skipped and
  `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` points at the docs worktree path. `collectTaskFiles`
  reads from the docs worktree. `commitAndPush` commits+pushes **both**
  worktrees (docs first or code first — D3 decides; recommend docs-first so a
  half-pushed state never shows code without its docs… or code-first — D3
  writes the rationale either way).

### 4.4 Auth (pending spike R1 — shape, not final)

- Backend git ops and runner `runGit` both rely on ambient credentials today
  (live `.git/config` remotes + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` fail-fast). The docs
  remote must authenticate the same way wherever possible (same host ⇒ same
  credential helper ⇒ zero new secrets UI).
- If R1 finds runners/hosts where ambient auth can't cover a second remote,
  add an optional per-project docs credential stored server-side, injected via
  `GIT_ASKPASS`/header at clone/fetch time, never persisted into `.git/config`,
  never logged (extend `redactCredentials` coverage + a redaction test).
- Hard rule: docs-repo credentials must never leak into the main repo, task
  docs, logs, or claim payloads. Spike R1 must name the exact mechanism before
  Phase 2 starts.

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
  its own design section (§7).

- `runner/project.js` — `prepareWorkdir({ repoUrl, localPath, workRoot,

### 3.4 Key invariants to preserve

1. **Single-branch resolvers**: `resolveDocsPath` / `resolveKainbainDir` stay
   the only place that maps (project, cwd) → absolute path. No caller
   hand-builds `cwd + "/docs"`.
2. **Redacted-at-rest URLs**: stored repo URLs are redacted; live git reads
   `.git/config` (see `detectGitRemote`, `redactCredentials`).
3. **Never-lose-work git hygiene**: recovery branches, no force-delete of
   unpushed work, `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction rules — the docs worktree inherits
   all of it.
4. **Runner ships standalone**: runner-side helpers cannot import backend code
   (the `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` duplication is intentional).
5. **Tolerant reads, strict writes**: resolvers degrade to defaults on garbage;
   write paths 400 with `INVALID_*` codes (see `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`

## 4. Target design (v1)

### 4.1 Data model — new project fields

```text
project.docsRepo: {
  url: string|null        # credential-REDACTED remote URL, e.g. "https://git.example.com/me/proj-kb.git"
  localPath: string|null  # backend-side checkout of the docs repo (absolute).
                          # For adopted/local setups: a path the operator gives or
                          # KainBain provisions next to cwd. For remote-backed: the
                          # backend's own clone/mirror location.
  branchMode: "synced"    # v1 fixed: docs repo carries the same kb/<taskId>
                          # branches as the code repo (see §4.3). Reserved for
                          # future "single-branch" mode.
  # auth: decided by research spike R1. Preferred: reuse the host's existing
  # credential mechanism per-remote (git credential helper / env), with an
  # optional per-project docs credential slot when R1 shows a gap.
}
```

- Absent `docsRepo` (legacy projects, default) = today's behaviour, byte for
  byte. This is the compatibility anchor: every new branch is `if
  (hasDocsRepo(project)) … else …today…`.
- Validation mirrors `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`:
  `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite` → 400 `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes; tolerant
  `normalizeDocsRepoSettings` for reads.
- One docs repo per project enforced (q7): backend refuses a `localPath`/`url`
  already claimed by another project (clear 409 message), until sharing is
  designed.

### 4.2 Backend layout — "KainBain home" split

Introduce one concept: **`kainbainHome/projectCwd` split**.

- Today: `projectCwd` serves as *both* code home and KainBain home
  (`<cwd>/docs/tasks`, `<cwd>/.kainbain/*`).
- With `docsRepo`: code home stays `projectCwd`; KainBain home becomes the
  docs-repo checkout (`docsRepo.localPath` on the backend).
- Implementation: add `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)` =
  `docsRepo.localPath || projectCwd`, then re-point `resolveDocsPath` and
  `resolveKainbainDir` at it (they already take `(cwd, project)` — the
  signature barely changes; internally `cwd` becomes "kainbain home").
  All downstream consumers (`taskDocsFiles`, `taskWorkspace`,
  `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `reportRelPath`, …) inherit the move with no edits —
  this is the "make change easy" payoff.
- `ensureDocsLink` / centralised-docs symlink: when `docsRepo` is set, the
  `<cwd>/docs` symlink is **not created** (stealth, q5) and
  `centralizedDocs` is ignored for that project (documented precedence:
  `docsRepo` > `centralizedDocs:false` > symlink). The docs checkout itself is
  a real git repo, not a symlink.
- `.gitignore` management: today KainBain writes ignore entries for
  `docs/tasks/` + `.kainbain/` into the main repo. With `docsRepo`, nothing is
  written into the main repo (q5 ★); equivalent ignores (if still needed) live
  in the docs repo. Audit every ignore-writing call site in Phase 1.
- `project.json`: per q1 ★, the authoritative copy lives in the docs repo
  (`<docsHome>/.kainbain/project.json`… or flattened — decided in Phase 1;
  recommend keeping the `.kainbain/` layout identical so resolvers don't fork).
  The backend's project *registry* (`projectRegistry.js`) keeps a pointer so
  `scanProjects` still finds the project. Main repo keeps zero files.

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
  its own design section (§7).

- `runner/project.js` — `prepareWorkdir({ repoUrl, localPath, workRoot,

### 3.4 Key invariants to preserve

1. **Single-branch resolvers**: `resolveDocsPath` / `resolveKainbainDir` stay
   the only place that maps (project, cwd) → absolute path. No caller
   hand-builds `cwd + "/docs"`.
2. **Redacted-at-rest URLs**: stored repo URLs are redacted; live git reads
   `.git/config` (see `detectGitRemote`, `redactCredentials`).
3. **Never-lose-work git hygiene**: recovery branches, no force-delete of
   unpushed work, `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction rules — the docs worktree inherits
   all of it.
4. **Runner ships standalone**: runner-side helpers cannot import backend code
   (the `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` duplication is intentional).
5. **Tolerant reads, strict writes**: resolvers degrade to defaults on garbage;
   write paths 400 with `INVALID_*` codes (see `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`
   pattern).

## 4. Target design (v1)

### 4.1 Data model — new project fields

```text
project.docsRepo: {
  url: string|null        # credential-REDACTED remote URL, e.g. "https://git.example.com/me/proj-kb.git"
  localPath: string|null  # backend-side checkout of the docs repo (absolute).
                          # For adopted/local setups: a path the operator gives or
                          # KainBain provisions next to cwd. For remote-backed: the
                          # backend's own clone/mirror location.
  branchMode: "synced"    # v1 fixed: docs repo carries the same kb/<taskId>
                          # branches as the code repo (see §4.3). Reserved for
                          # future "single-branch" mode.
  # auth: decided by research spike R1. Preferred: reuse the host's existing
  # credential mechanism per-remote (git credential helper / env), with an
  # optional per-project docs credential slot when R1 shows a gap.
}
```

- Absent `docsRepo` (legacy projects, default) = today's behaviour, byte for
  byte. This is the compatibility anchor: every new branch is `if
  (hasDocsRepo(project)) … else …today…`.
- Validation mirrors `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`:
  `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite` → 400 `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes; tolerant
  `normalizeDocsRepoSettings` for reads.
- One docs repo per project enforced (q7): backend refuses a `localPath`/`url`
  already claimed by another project (clear 409 message), until sharing is
  designed.

### 4.2 Backend layout — "KainBain home" split

Introduce one concept: **`kainbainHome/projectCwd` split**.

- Today: `projectCwd` serves as *both* code home and KainBain home
  (`<cwd>/docs/tasks`, `<cwd>/.kainbain/*`).
- With `docsRepo`: code home stays `projectCwd`; KainBain home becomes the
  docs-repo checkout (`docsRepo.localPath` on the backend).
- Implementation: add `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)` =
  `docsRepo.localPath || projectCwd`, then re-point `resolveDocsPath` and
  `resolveKainbainDir` at it (they already take `(cwd, project)` — the
  signature barely changes; internally `cwd` becomes "kainbain home").
  All downstream consumers (`taskDocsFiles`, `taskWorkspace`,
  `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `reportRelPath`, …) inherit the move with no edits —
  this is the "make change easy" payoff.
- `ensureDocsLink` / centralised-docs symlink: when `docsRepo` is set, the
  `<cwd>/docs` symlink is **not created** (stealth, q5) and
  `centralizedDocs` is ignored for that project (documented precedence:
  `docsRepo` > `centralizedDocs:false` > symlink). The docs checkout itself is
  a real git repo, not a symlink.
- `.gitignore` management: today KainBain writes ignore entries for
  `docs/tasks/` + `.kainbain/` into the main repo. With `docsRepo`, nothing is
  written into the main repo (q5 ★); equivalent ignores (if still needed) live
  in the docs repo. Audit every ignore-writing call site in Phase 1.
- `project.json`: per q1 ★, the authoritative copy lives in the docs repo
  (`<docsHome>/.kainbain/project.json`… or flattened — decided in Phase 1;
  recommend keeping the `.kainbain/` layout identical so resolvers don't fork).
  The backend's project *registry* (`projectRegistry.js`) keeps a pointer so
  `scanProjects` still finds the project. Main repo keeps zero files.

### 4.3 Branching — synced task branches across two repos

- The docs repo carries the **same branch names** as the code repo:
  `kb/<taskId>` per task, same default branch. "Synced" means: created from
  the same base event, checked out/created together at stage pickup
  (`ensureTaskBranch` gains a docs-repo twin), and pushed together at handoff.
- Merge/review semantics stay code-repo-driven: the Merge stage merges code;
  docs branches merge (or fast-forward) alongside so docs history tracks task
  history. Exact merge coupling (same commit message? docs-merge part of the
  merge stage, or lazy?) is decided in design task D3 (Phase 1) — v1 default:
  docs branch is merged/fast-forwarded by the same stage right after the code
  merge, failures reported but never blocking the code merge verdict… or
  blocking — D3 decides with a written rationale.
- Runner workdir layout becomes a pair:
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` (code worktree, as today) +
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>-docs` (docs worktree, same branch name), each with
  its own mirror (`mirrors/<code-slug>`, `mirrors/<docs-slug>`).
  `prepareWorkdir` grows a `docsRepoUrl` option; eviction/recovery/reap logic
  treats the pair atomically (evict/reap both, park both).
- `syncTaskDocs` becomes a no-op source change: with docsRepo, task docs live
  *in* the docs worktree already — the copy step is skipped and
  `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` points at the docs worktree path. `collectTaskFiles`
  reads from the docs worktree. `commitAndPush` commits+pushes **both**
  worktrees (docs first or code first — D3 decides; recommend docs-first so a
  half-pushed state never shows code without its docs… or code-first — D3
  writes the rationale either way).

### 4.4 Auth (pending spike R1 — shape, not final)

- Backend git ops and runner `runGit` both rely on ambient credentials today
  (live `.git/config` remotes + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` fail-fast). The docs
  remote must authenticate the same way wherever possible (same host ⇒ same
  credential helper ⇒ zero new secrets UI).
- If R1 finds runners/hosts where ambient auth can't cover a second remote,
  add an optional per-project docs credential stored server-side, injected via
  `GIT_ASKPASS`/header at clone/fetch time, never persisted into `.git/config`,
  never logged (extend `redactCredentials` coverage + a redaction test).
- Hard rule: docs-repo credentials must never leak into the main repo, task
  docs, logs, or claim payloads. Spike R1 must name the exact mechanism before
  Phase 2 starts.

user-visible behaviour last; each phase is independently shippable and leaves
the tree green.** Big/risky pieces (two-repo execution model, auth) are
investigated in Phase 0 before any behaviour changes.

### Phase 1 — Make change easy (backend seams, no behaviour change)

Goal: after Phase 1, switching a project's KainBain home is a **one-line
resolver change**, fully covered by tests, with zero user-visible difference.

- **D1. Introduce `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)`** (new module,
  e.g. `api/kainbainHome.js`, mirroring `docsPath.js`/`kainbainDir.js`
  conventions incl. JSDoc `MARK:` blocks). Initially returns `projectCwd`
  always. Re-point `resolveDocsPath` and `resolveKainbainDir` internals at it.
  Unit tests: legacy projects unchanged; explicit cases for the future
  docs-home branch (written now, enabled when the field exists).
- **D2. Fix census strays (from R3)**: route any hand-built docs/state paths
  through the resolvers. Each fix: regression test proving identical output
  before/after.
- **D3. Write the two-repo execution ADR** (design doc under `docs/`):
  branch-sync coupling, merge-stage semantics, commit/push order, failure
  taxonomy (what happens when docs push fails but code push succeeds, and vice
  versa), `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` contract, `taskFiles`/`taskAssets` source of
  truth. Review the ADR before Phase 2 — it is the spec Phase 2/3 implement.
- **D4. Validation/normalisation scaffolding**: add `api/project/docsRepo.js`
  with `normalizeDocsRepoSettings` (tolerant) + `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite`
  (strict, `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes) + `hasDocsRepo(project)`, following the
  `docsDirName`/`kainbainDirName` pattern. Wire into create/update validation
  behind the new fields but accept-and-ignore until Phase 2 enables storage
  (or store-but-ignore — D4 decides; must be invisible either way). Unit tests
  for validators now.
- **D5. Runner seam prep**: extract the single-repo assumptions in
  `prepareWorkdir`/`syncTaskDocs`/`collectTaskFiles` behind small helpers
  (`docsWorkdirFor(workdir)`, `shouldSyncTaskDocs(project)`) that return
  today's values. No behaviour change; runner unit tests stay green.

Phase 1 exit criteria: `npm run test:unit` green; new unit tests for D1/D4/D5
pass; ADR (D3) written and reviewed; R2 checklist fully mapped to D-tasks or
Phase 2/3 tasks.

### Phase 2 — Backend: docs-repo projects (the change, part 1)

- **B1. Persist + validate `project.docsRepo`** (`createProject`,
  `registerProject`, `PATCH`): strict validation (D4), 409 on already-claimed
  URL/localPath (q7), redacted URL at rest. Route tests copying
  `projects.docsSettings.test.js` patterns.
- **B2. Provisioning**: on create-with-docsRepo, `git init`/clone the docs
  checkout at `docsRepo.localPath`, lay out `.kainbain/` + `docs/tasks/`
  skeleton, write `project.json` there (q1 ★), register the pointer so
  `scanProjects` finds it. On adopt-with-docsRepo, verify the given local path
  (must exist, must be a git repo or empty dir — fail loud otherwise). **Write
  nothing into the main repo** (R2 checklist enforced by test: snapshot the
  main repo tree before/after provisioning).
- **B3. Flip `resolveKainbainHome`**: return `docsRepo.localPath` when set.
  All docs/state consumers move at once. `ensureDocsLink`: docsRepo projects
  report a new state (e.g. `'external-docs'`) and never touch `<cwd>/docs`.
  Centralised-docs precedence documented + tested.
- **B4. Git ops for the docs repo**: clone/fetch/checkout/push helpers for the
  docs checkout reusing `api/git/*` + `withRepoGitLock` equivalents;
  `ensureTaskBranch` gains its docs twin (create/checkout `kb/<taskId>` in
  docs repo alongside code repo); main/task sync helpers (`syncMain…`,
  `syncTaskBranch…`) run for both repos per ADR D3. Dirty-tree guards apply to
  both checkouts.
- **B5. Merge/review/deploy integration** per ADR: merge stage merges both
  branches; review diff stays code-driven (docs diff optionally linked —
  decide in D3); deploy packaging excludes docs checkout (verify: no docs leak
  into deploy artefacts).
- **B6. Back-compat & safety**: legacy projects (no `docsRepo`) byte-identical
  behaviour — full existing suite must pass unmodified. Enabling docsRepo on a
  project with existing docs: q4 ★ = leave old docs in place, new writes go to
  docs repo; surface a settings banner noting the split + link to the manual
  move procedure (docs task, Phase 5). Disabling docsRepo: refuse while docs
  branches are ahead/unpushed (fail loud with the recovery command), else flip
  back.

Phase 2 exit criteria: backend unit + integration tests green (old + new);
main-repo-cleanliness tests pass (B2/R2); two-repo branch sync covered by
integration tests with throwaway git repos.

### Phase 3 — Runner: adjacent docs checkout + synced branches (the change, part 2)

- **C1. `prepareWorkdir` + docs pair**: new `docsRepoUrl`/`docsLocalPath`
  options; mirror `mirrors/<docs-slug>`; worktree `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>-docs`
  on the same `kb/<taskId>` branch; reuse `runGit`/`refreshMirror`/
  `refreshWorktreeToRemote` paths (no second git implementation). Reuse +
  LRU eviction + reap treat the pair atomically.
- **C2. Docs flow in the worktree pair**: skip `syncTaskDocs` copy when the
  docs worktree is present (docs already there); `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` points at
  the docs worktree; `writeClaimTaskAssets` writes into the docs worktree;
  `collectTaskFiles` reads from it. Stage prompts' `./docs/tasks/…` relative
  paths keep working because the agent's cwd mapping is updated accordingly
  (detail in ADR D3 — likely: agent runs in code worktree, docs worktree path
  exported + symlinked read view… or agent cwd unchanged with docs bind — D3
  decides; the requirement is that existing prompt relative paths don't break).
- **C3. `commitAndPush` both worktrees** per ADR order; integrate-upstream for
  both; conflict taxonomy extended (`sync-conflict` names which repo).
  Recovery parking (`kb-recovery/*`) covers both worktrees.
- **C4. Remote-runner (no primary checkout) path**: claim payloads already
  carry `taskAssets`; extend the claim/dispatch contract with the docs remote
  URL (+ credential ref per R1) so a remote runner can clone both mirrors.
  Back-compat: old runners ignore the new claim fields (or are version-gated —
  decide in D3; must not break mixed fleets silently).
- **C5. Runner unit + integration tests**: paired layout, eviction atomicity,
  reuse refresh of both worktrees, push-order, conflict attribution, cap
  accounting (does the pair count as 1 or 2 against `WORKTREE_CAP`? — D3
  decides; recommend 1 pair = 1 slot).

Phase 3 exit criteria: runner test files green (`runner/*.test.js`); an
end-to-end throwaway run (two local remotes, clone-mode runner) completes a
task with docs landing only in the docs remote.

+

Standards file: `docs/KB Code Standards.md`, read together with its referenced detailed copy `docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md` (§Documentation/Jsdoc). This stage is docs-only; no source was modified — this review was produced by read-only inspection and test runs.

+## Scope reviewed (`git diff main...HEAD --stat`)

+- `runner/client.js` (+53) — new `TRANSIENT_BACKEND_STATUSES`, `TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES`, exported `isTransientBackendError(err)`.
+- `runner/daemon.js` (+159) — new `retryTransient`, `describeBackendOutageCause`; transient branches in `joinAndHeartbeat`, `executeAssignment`, `executeIntegrationAssignment`, `runSingleAssignment`, `runDispatchLoop`.
+- `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (new, 202 lines), `runner/daemon.test.js` (+580), `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (registration), `publish.sh` (runner gate registration), `runner/README.md` (failure-handling note), `runner/version.json` (`0.2.0` -> `0.2.1`).
+- Task docs under `docs/tasks/78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e/` (implementation plan, survey, upgrade-safety review, two auto-generated reports).
+
+The diff does **not** restructure the db49d6c6 dispatch-loop catch, per the MUST-READ constraint — verified by grep of the `runner/daemon.js` diff (only additive branches; the `else { throw err }` tail and `STALE_EPOCH` propagation remain).
+
+## Verdict: PASS — no blocking standards violation found
+
+Each standard below was checked against the actual diff and test runs. Minor observations are listed as notes, not failures.
+
+### Values — user understandable over technical language
+
+- **Long descriptive names — pass.** New identifiers are descriptive: `TRANSIENT_BACKEND_STATUSES`, `TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES`, `describeBackendOutageCause`, `retryTransient`, `callBackend`, `waitsMs`. The user-facing interrupt reason is plain English: `` `Backend unreachable mid-assignment: ${...}` `` (`runner/daemon.js:2513`, `:2787`) and the dispatch log `Dispatch: backend unreachable (...)` — no invented abstractions.
+- **Technical language — pass.** No new "factory"/"barrel"/pattern vocabulary. A case-insensitive grep for `factory|Singleton|Strategy|Observer|design pattern` over `runner/client.js` + `runner/daemon.js` finds only the pre-existing comment "module singleton" (`runner/daemon.js:1055`), untouched by this branch. The word "transient" is the domain term from the task brief, used consistently with the test file header (`GUIDE-04 section 2/3` references) and `runner/README.md`.
+- **Common language profile — pass.** `task`, `assignment`, `runner`, `backend`, `interrupt` are used in their established senses; nothing is renamed.
+- **File structure reflects call stack — pass.** The classifier lives in `runner/client.js` (the file that defines the `{ statusCode, code }` vs raw-fetch-rejection error shapes) and `runner/daemon.js` imports it (`runner/daemon.js:47`). This is the correct call-hierarchy direction (daemon -> client), not an inversion.
+- **JSDoc plain English + `@example` + MARK — pass, gate-verified.** Every new export/helper carries `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example` + `@param`/`@returns`:
+  - `MARK: isTransientBackendError` (`runner/client.js:24-38`) with `@example isTransientBackendError(Object.assign(new Error('x'), { statusCode: 502 })) => true`,
+  - `MARK: retryTransient` (`runner/daemon.js:1106-1121`),
+  - `MARK: describeBackendOutageCause` (`runner/daemon.js:1135-1149`),

Not a failing violation.

+
+- **Tests next to the file — pass.** New `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` sits beside `runner/client.js`; daemon boundary tests are appended in `runner/daemon.test.js` beside the existing `runDispatchLoop`/`runSingleAssignment` blocks, reusing `stubClient`/`fakeHarness`/`loopConfig`.

Both mirror an existing sibling shape (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` report-and-return, 429/`RUNNER_PAUSED` backoff) rather than inventing a layer.
+- **Searchability — pass.** `isTransientBackendError` is the single grep-able home for the non-fatal set; all four catch sites call it. No status/close-code checks are duplicated inline.

+
+- **Tests planned and evidenced — pass, verified by execution in this review:**
+  - `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` -> 9 pass / 0 fail (classifier boundary: gateway positives, socket-code positives incl. nested/cyclic causes, STALE_EPOCH/auth/429/500/501 negatives, bare-`fetch failed` stays loud; wire shapes: 502 json + proxy-HTML, 503/504, dropped socket, recovery).
+  - `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` -> 180 pass / 0 fail, including the S4 boundary tests (transient returns with interrupt-with-reason and loop keeps polling; STALE_EPOCH/auth/unknown still rethrow; join ride-through and exhaustion; dispatch backoff without consuming idle budget; integration parity).
+  - `node --test runner/client.test.js` -> 16 pass / 0 fail (no disturbance to existing client shapes).
+  - Registration pins now green: `node --test tests/publish.test.mjs tests/run-tests.test.mjs` -> 68 pass / 0 fail. (The earlier `automated-tests-failure-20261123-092217.md` Harness-Self-Tests failure was the `publish.sh` runner gate missing the new suite; the current HEAD registers it in both `scripts/run-tests.mjs` and `publish.sh` and the pin passes — resolved, not open.)
+- **Lowest level first, black-box, user-shaped — pass.** The outage suite exercises the real `createRunnerClient.call` path with a stubbed `fetchImpl` (GUIDE-04 §2 shapes); daemon tests drive real `runDispatchLoop`/`runSingleAssignment` with temp git repos and a fake harness (lowest level that proves the loop behavior; no live AI agent, no ports). +- **Fatality boundary is explicit — pass.** The classifier enumerates 502/503/504 + named network codes and falls through to false for everything else (STALE_EPOCH 409, 401/403, 429, 500, 501, unknown, non-thrown values). Tests pin both sides, including the flipped-red boundary (`rethrown === false` transient / `true` stale-epoch) by behavior, so new failure modes stay loud by construction.

239|/***
240| * MARK: scoreWord
241| * @description Scores one index entry against a single normalized word: 3 for
242| *   a label prefix match, 2 for a label substring, 1 for a keyword
243| *   substring, 0 for no match. Scores rank `searchSettings` so label hits
244| *   lead. A non-array `keywords` field scores 0 instead of throwing.
245| * @example scoreWord({ label: 'Git Repository URL', keywords: ['git'] }, 'git') => 3
246| * @param {Object} entry - One `SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX` entry.
247| * @param {string} word - Lowercase query word.
248| * @returns {number} Match score (0 = no match).
249| ***/
250|const scoreWord = (entry, word) => {
251|  const label = String(entry?.label ?? '').toLowerCase();
252|  if (label.startsWith(word)) return 3;
253|  if (label.includes(word)) return 2;
254|  const keywords = Array.isArray(entry?.keywords) ? entry.keywords : [];

256|  return 0;

260| * MARK: searchSettings

262| *   Multi-word queries match when EVERY word hits (label substring or
263| *   keyword substring), so "centralised docs folder" finds the docs-link
264| *   setting however the words are ordered. Scores sum the per-word best
265| *   hits, best matches first with index order breaking ties. Blank queries
266| *   and non-matches return an empty array.

271|export const searchSettings = (query) => {
272|  const normalized = String(query ?? '')
273|    .trim()
274|    .toLowerCase();
275|  if (!normalized) return [];
276|  const words = normalized.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
277|  return SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX.map((entry, index) => {
278|    let score = 0;
279|    for (const word of words) {
280|      const wordScore = scoreWord(entry, word);
281|      // One missed word disqualifies the entry (AND semantics).
282|      if (wordScore === 0) return null;
283|      score += wordScore;
284|    }
285|    return { entry, score, index };
286|  })
287|    .filter((hit) => hit !== null)
288|    .sort((first, second) => second.score - first.score || first.index - second.index)
289|    .map((hit) => hit.entry);
290|};

297| * @param {string} query - Raw user input.
298| * @returns {Object|null} The best matching entry, if any.
299| ***/
300|export const findBestMatch = (query) => searchSettings(query)[0] ?? null;

Read text file `docs/tasks/7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
1|# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project
2|
3|Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
4|Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
5|Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)
6|
7|## 1. Goal and non-goals
8|
9|**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
10|private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:
11|
12|- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
13|- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
14|- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
15|- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
16|  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
17|- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
18|  (especially on import).
19|
20|**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):
21|
22|- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
23|  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
24|- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
25|  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
26|  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
27|- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
28|  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
29|  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
30|  its own design section (§7).
31|
32|## 2. Survey analysis (SURVEY.md) — unanswered, with recommendations
33|
34|The grill survey exists but `answers` is `{}` — nobody has answered yet. The
35|plan below assumes the **recommended** answer for each question (marked ★) and
36|notes where the code must keep the other option open. Before implementation
37|starts, re-run the grill (or get 5 minutes of the requester's time) to confirm;
38|each recommendation is one line to flip.
39|
40|| # | Question | Recommended answer ★ | Why / plan impact |
41||---|----------|----------------------|-------------------|
42|| q1 | What lives in the docs repo? | ★ **Everything KainBain**: task docs (`docs/tasks/*`), plans, reports, **and** KainBain settings/state (`.kainbain/` contents: `project.json`, sessions, worktrees, quarantine) | Stealth requires zero KainBain traces in the main repo (q5). Splitting settings from docs would leave a decision matrix in every resolver. One "KainBain home" location keeps `resolveDocsPath`/`resolveKainbainDir` a single-branch change. If q1 instead resolves to "task docs only", Phase 3 still works: `project.json` stays in main repo and only the docs resolvers move — the seam is the same. |
43|| q2 | Where in the import/create UI? | ★ **Tucked under an 'Advanced' section** on *both* create and import dialogs | Task text says "as an advance option" and "allowed from the default when you import/create". Advanced-collapsed keeps the simple form simple (existing dialogs are minimal: name+remote, path+name) while satisfying "from the default". Also add the same fields to Project Settings (Paths & Repositories) so it can be enabled later. |
44|| q3 | Auth for the (private) docs repo? | ★ **Separate login details just for the docs repo** (stored credential, optional: fall back to same-as-main when blank) | Main repo may be public/shared with no credential while docs repo is private, or the two live on different hosts. Design a `docsRepo` credential slot reusing the existing credential-redaction + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` patterns; empty = "same as main repo" keeps the simple case one field. Research spike R1 (Phase 0) must confirm the current credential flow first. |
45|| q4 | Existing docs when switching on? | ★ **Leave old docs; only new work goes to the separate repo** (+ documented manual move command) | Auto-move is a data-loss-risky migration (symlink/shadow history — see `ensureDocsLink` incident note). Leave-in-place is safe, reversible, and matches "make change easy then make the change". Auto-move becomes a follow-up stage with its own backup/verify semantics. |
46|| q5 | Main repo completely free of traces? | ★ **Yes — nothing KainBain-related in the main repo** | This is the stated stealth goal ("so I can stealth use kainbain at work"). Consequences: no `.kainbain/` dir, no `docs/tasks/` content, no pointer file, and (v1) `.gitignore` entries must also not be written into the main repo — they move into the docs repo / global config. The task text's "tiny pointer file is fine" alternative is explicitly rejected for v1 because any committed file defeats stealth. |
47|| q6 | Keep `kb/*` working branches out of shared repo too? | ★ **No — branches in the main repo are fine for v1; only docs/state move** (with a designed follow-up) | True branch stealth (code work happening in a fork/private mirror + PRs back) is a fundamentally different execution model (merge/push/review paths all assume `kb/<task>` exists on origin). V1 separates docs; §7 sketches the branch-stealth follow-up. If the requester insists on full stealth for v1, the plan gains ~2 extra phases — escalate before starting. |
48|| q7 | One docs repo per project, or shared? | ★ **One docs repo per project only (v1)** | Sharing needs namespacing (`<docsRepo>/<projectSlug>/tasks/...`), cross-project locking, and quota/permission questions. Single-project keeps every resolver a pure path swap. Design the on-disk layout with a namespaced root anyway (`tasks/` at top level today, reservable for `<slug>/` prefix later) so sharing is additive. |
49|
50|**Action before Phase 1:** confirm q1–q7 with the requester (5-minute grill
51|re-run). If any answer flips, only the flagged phase changes — the Phase 0/1
52|seams are answer-independent by design.
53|
54|## 3. Current-state findings (grounded in the repo)
55|
56|All paths below are relative to the repo root. This is the surface the plan
57|must move:
58|
59|### 3.1 Backend — project identity and docs location
60|
61|- `api/projectStore.js` — `ProjectStore`: filesystem-backed projects. Key
62|  fields on the project record: `cwd` (main checkout), `notesPath`/`notesDir`,
63|  `docsDirName` (default `docs`), `centralizedDocs` (default true),
64|  `kainbainDirName` (default `.kainbain`), `gitUrl`/`repoUrl`, `useBranches`.
65|  `createProject` / `registerProject` provision; `ensureDocsLink` verifies the
66|  `<cwd>/<docsDir>/ → notes-space` symlink with careful repair policy.
67|- `api/docsPath.js` — **the docs seam**: `resolveDocsDirName`,
68|  `isCentralizedDocsEnabled`, `normalizeDocsSettings`,
69|  `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`, `resolveDocsPath(cwd, project)`,
70|  `resolveTasksDir`, `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `docsProjectFor`,
71|  `reportRelPath`, `docsTasksIgnorePath`. Every task-docs path flows through
72|  here. ★ This is where "make change easy" concentrates.
73|- `api/kainbainDir.js` — **the state seam**: mirrors `docsPath.js` for
74|  `<cwd>/.kainbain/` (`resolveKainbainDir`, `resolveProjectConfigPath`,
75|  `resolveSessionsDir`, `resolveWorktreesDir`, `resolveQuarantineDir`,
76|  `kainbainIgnorePath`). Per q1-recommended, both seams move together.
77|- `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js`, `api/work/taskAssets.js`,
78|  `api/work/taskWorkspace.js` (`repairDocsLinkAfterSwitch`,
79|  `resolveTaskCwd`, quarantine/worktree dirs), `api/work/taskBranches.js`
80|  (`kb/<taskId>` branches, worktree isolation, main/task sync helpers),
81|  `api/work/resolveProjectCwd.js` — all take `projectCwd` and derive docs/state
82|  paths from it. They must learn "docs home ≠ code home" without changing
83|  call signatures more than necessary.
84|- `api/project/gitRemote.js` — `resolveDefaultGitRemote` (template-based),
85|  `detectGitRemote` (reads `remote.origin.url`, **credential-redacted** via
86|  `redactCredentials`; git ops read the live remote from `.git/config`, never
87|  the stored value). The docs repo needs the same treatment: stored URL
88|  redacted, live URL from its own `.git/config`.
89|- `api/routes/projects.js` — `POST /projects` (create), `POST
90|  /projects/register` (adopt), `PATCH` (settings incl. docs settings —
91|  `projects.docsSettings.test.js`, `projects.kainbainDir.test.js` show the
92|  established validation/test pattern to copy).
93|
94|### 3.2 Runner — adjacent checkout and synced branches
95|
96|- `runner/project.js` — `prepareWorkdir({ repoUrl, localPath, workRoot,
97|  taskId })`: clone-mode mirror at `<workRoot>/mirrors/<slug>` (+
98|  `refreshMirror`) or adopt-mode local path; per-task worktree
99|  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` on branch `kb/<taskId>` (+
100|  `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, LRU eviction under `WORKTREE_CAP`,
101|  `kb-recovery/*` parking). `syncTaskDocs` copies
102|  `<primaryCwd>/docs/tasks/<id>` into the worktree; `writeClaimTaskAssets`
103|  covers remote runners; `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` mirrors the backend
104|  resolver (deliberately duplicated — "the Runner ships without the backend
105|  tree"). `collectTaskFiles` in `runner/daemon.js` ships worktree files back.
106|- `runner/gitOps.js` — `commitAndPush` / `integrateUpstream`: stage-end handoff
107|  pushes the worktree (code + docs together today).
108|- Runner git runs with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, 60s budget, per-workdir
109|  serialisation, stale-lock recovery (`RunnerGitError` codes). The docs
110|  checkout must reuse `runGit`, not invent a second git path.
111|- Runner ↔ backend file transfer for task docs goes through the worktree +
112|  claim payloads (`taskFiles`, `taskAssets`), not through direct docs-repo
113|  access — this is what lets a remote runner work with no primary checkout.
114|
115|### 3.3 Frontend — create/import/settings
116|
117|- `frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx` — New Project modal (name + git
118|  remote) and Add Existing Project modal (path + display name + KainBain
119|  folder). No "Advanced" disclosure exists yet — one must be added (q2).
120|- `frontend/src/components/settings/PathsAndReposSection.jsx` (+
121|  `ProjectSettingsForm.jsx`) — Files & Repositories block: cwd, notes symlink,
122|  docs folder name, KainBain folder name, centralised-docs toggle, git URL,
123|  task-branch options. This is where the docs-repo URL + credential fields land
124|  for existing projects.
125|
126|### 3.4 Key invariants to preserve
127|
128|1. **Single-branch resolvers**: `resolveDocsPath` / `resolveKainbainDir` stay
129|   the only place that maps (project, cwd) → absolute path. No caller
130|   hand-builds `cwd + "/docs"`.
131|2. **Redacted-at-rest URLs**: stored repo URLs are redacted; live git reads
132|   `.git/config` (see `detectGitRemote`, `redactCredentials`).
133|3. **Never-lose-work git hygiene**: recovery branches, no force-delete of
134|   unpushed work, `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction rules — the docs worktree inherits
135|   all of it.
136|4. **Runner ships standalone**: runner-side helpers cannot import backend code
137|   (the `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` duplication is intentional).
138|5. **Tolerant reads, strict writes**: resolvers degrade to defaults on garbage;
139|   write paths 400 with `INVALID_*` codes (see `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`
140|   pattern).
141|
142|## 4. Target design (v1)
143|
144|### 4.1 Data model — new project fields
145|
146|```text
147|project.docsRepo: {
148|  url: string|null        # credential-REDACTED remote URL, e.g. "https://git.example.com/me/proj-kb.git"
149|  localPath: string|null  # backend-side checkout of the docs repo (absolute).
150|                          # For adopted/local setups: a path the operator gives or
151|                          # KainBain provisions next to cwd. For remote-backed: the
152|                          # backend's own clone/mirror location.
153|  branchMode: "synced"    # v1 fixed: docs repo carries the same kb/<taskId>

179|  docs-repo checkout (`docsRepo.localPath` on the backend).

181|  `docsRepo.localPath || projectCwd`, then re-point `resolveDocsPath` and

191|  a real git repo, not a symlink.

193|  `docs/tasks/` + `.kainbain/` into the main repo. With `docsRepo`, nothing is

7|## 1. Goal and non-goals
8|
9|**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
10|private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:
11|
12|- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;

143|
144|### 4.1 Data model — new project fields
145|
146|```text
147|project.docsRepo: {
148|  url: string|null        # credential-REDACTED remote URL, e.g. "https://git.example.com/me/proj-kb.git"
149|  localPath: string|null  # backend-side checkout of the docs repo (absolute).
150|                          # For adopted/local setups: a path the operator gives or
151|                          # KainBain provisions next to cwd. For remote-backed: the
152|                          # backend's own clone/mirror location.
153|  branchMode: "synced"    # v1 fixed: docs repo carries the same kb/<taskId>
154|                          # branches as the code repo (see §4.3). Reserved for
155|                          # future "single-branch" mode.
156|  # auth: decided by research spike R1. Preferred: reuse the host's existing
157|  # credential mechanism per-remote (git credential helper / env), with an
158|  # optional per-project docs credential slot when R1 shows a gap.
159|}
160|```
161|
162|- Absent `docsRepo` (legacy projects, default) = today's behaviour, byte for
163|  byte. This is the compatibility anchor: every new branch is `if
164|  (hasDocsRepo(project)) … else …today…`.
165|- Validation mirrors `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`:
166|  `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite` → 400 `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes; tolerant
167|  `normalizeDocsRepoSettings` for reads.
168|- One docs repo per project enforced (q7): backend refuses a `localPath`/`url`
169|  already claimed by another project (clear 409 message), until sharing is
170|  designed.

172|### 4.2 Backend layout — "KainBain home" split
173|
174|Introduce one concept: **`kainbainHome/projectCwd` split**.
175|
176|- Today: `projectCwd` serves as *both* code home and KainBain home
177|  (`<cwd>/docs/tasks`, `<cwd>/.kainbain/*`).
178|- With `docsRepo`: code home stays `projectCwd`; KainBain home becomes the
179|  docs-repo checkout (`docsRepo.localPath` on the backend).
180|- Implementation: add `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)` =
181|  `docsRepo.localPath || projectCwd`, then re-point `resolveDocsPath` and
182|  `resolveKainbainDir` at it (they already take `(cwd, project)` — the
183|  signature barely changes; internally `cwd` becomes "kainbain home").
184|  All downstream consumers (`taskDocsFiles`, `taskWorkspace`,
185|  `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `reportRelPath`, …) inherit the move with no edits —
186|  this is the "make change easy" payoff.
187|- `ensureDocsLink` / centralised-docs symlink: when `docsRepo` is set, the
188|  `<cwd>/docs` symlink is **not created** (stealth, q5) and
189|  `centralizedDocs` is ignored for that project (documented precedence:
190|  `docsRepo` > `centralizedDocs:false` > symlink). The docs checkout itself is
191|  a real git repo, not a symlink.
192|- `.gitignore` management: today KainBain writes ignore entries for
193|  `docs/tasks/` + `.kainbain/` into the main repo. With `docsRepo`, nothing is
194|  written into the main repo (q5 ★); equivalent ignores (if still needed) live
195|  in the docs repo. Audit every ignore-writing call site in Phase 1.
196|- `project.json`: per q1 ★, the authoritative copy lives in the docs repo
197|  (`<docsHome>/.kainbain/project.json`… or flattened — decided in Phase 1;
198|  recommend keeping the `.kainbain/` layout identical so resolvers don't fork).
199|  The backend's project *registry* (`projectRegistry.js`) keeps a pointer so
200|  `scanProjects` still finds the project. Main repo keeps zero files.
201|
202|### 4.3 Branching — synced task branches across two repos
203|
204|- The docs repo carries the **same branch names** as the code repo:
205|  `kb/<taskId>` per task, same default branch. "Synced" means: created from
206|  the same base event, checked out/created together at stage pickup
207|  (`ensureTaskBranch` gains a docs-repo twin), and pushed together at handoff.
208|- Merge/review semantics stay code-repo-driven: the Merge stage merges code;
209|  docs branches merge (or fast-forward) alongside so docs history tracks task
210|  history. Exact merge coupling (same commit message? docs-merge part of the
211|  merge stage, or lazy?) is decided in design task D3 (Phase 1) — v1 default:
212|  docs branch is merged/fast-forwarded by the same stage right after the code
213|  merge, failures reported but never blocking the code merge verdict… or
214|  blocking — D3 decides with a written rationale.
215|- Runner workdir layout becomes a pair:
216|  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` (code worktree, as today) +
217|  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>-docs` (docs worktree, same branch name), each with
218|  its own mirror (`mirrors/<code-slug>`, `mirrors/<docs-slug>`).
219|  `prepareWorkdir` grows a `docsRepoUrl` option; eviction/recovery/reap logic
220|  treats the pair atomically (evict/reap both, park both).
221|- `syncTaskDocs` becomes a no-op source change: with docsRepo, task docs live
222|  *in* the docs worktree already — the copy step is skipped and
223|  `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` points at the docs worktree path. `collectTaskFiles`
224|  reads from the docs worktree. `commitAndPush` commits+pushes **both**
225|  worktrees (docs first or code first — D3 decides; recommend docs-first so a
226|  half-pushed state never shows code without its docs… or code-first — D3
227|  writes the rationale either way).
228|

230|
231|- Backend git ops and runner `runGit` both rely on ambient credentials today
232|  (live `.git/config` remotes + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` fail-fast). The docs
233|  remote must authenticate the same way wherever possible (same host ⇒ same
234|  credential helper ⇒ zero new secrets UI).
